title: Minor and Major Penalties Under CCS (CCA) Rules
description: Rule 11 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 lists 5 minor penalties, such as censure, and 5 major ones, up to dismissal. See the full list and procedure.
applies_to: Central Government civilian employees governed by the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965. Delhi Police subordinate ranks have their own list under the Delhi Police (Punishment and Appeal) Rules, 1980.
answer: Rule 11 of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965 has five minor penalties: censure, withholding promotion, recovery of loss from pay, a one-stage pay reduction of up to three years without cumulative effect, and withholding increments. The five major penalties are larger pay reductions, reduction to a lower scale or post, compulsory retirement, removal and dismissal.

sections.heading: The Minor Penalties
The Major Penalties
Actions That Are Not Penalties
Who Can Impose Them and How
sections.body_md:
The President may impose any Rule 11 penalty on any Government servant [(Rule 12(1), PDF p. 12)](https://dopt.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCS-CCA-Rules-FINAL.pdf#page=12). No authority subordinate to the appointing authority can impose a major penalty, with one limited exception for the Indian Audit and Accounts Service [(Rule 12(4)(a), PDF p. 13)](https://dopt.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCS-CCA-Rules-FINAL.pdf#page=13).

A major penalty needs a full inquiry under Rules 14 and 15 [(Rule 14(1), PDF p. 14)](https://dopt.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCS-CCA-Rules-FINAL.pdf#page=14). A minor penalty needs written notice of the proposal and the imputations, and a reasonable chance for you to represent [(Rule 16(1), PDF p. 23)](https://dopt.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCS-CCA-Rules-FINAL.pdf#page=23). An inquiry is compulsory even for withholding increments if it is likely to affect your pension, exceeds three years, or has cumulative effect [(Rule 16(1-A), PDF p. 23)](https://dopt.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCS-CCA-Rules-FINAL.pdf#page=23).

Delhi Police subordinate ranks are not covered by this list. The Delhi Police Act, 1978 penalties set out in Rule 5 of the Delhi Police (Punishment and Appeal) Rules, 1980 include dismissal, removal, reduction in rank, forfeiture of approved service, reduction in pay, withholding of increments, fine up to one month's pay, censure, and punishment drill for constables [(DP (P&A) Rule 5, PDF p. 17)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=17).

sections.heading: Where to Check
sections.body_md:
- Rule 11 (penalties) and Rule 12 (disciplinary authorities) of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, DoPT copy updated up to 15.10.2018 [(CCS (CCA) Rules, cover, PDF p. 1)](https://dopt.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCS-CCA-Rules-FINAL.pdf#page=1).
- Rules 14 to 16 for the procedure [(Rule 14, PDF p. 14)](https://dopt.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCS-CCA-Rules-FINAL.pdf#page=14).
- For Delhi Police, Rules 5 and 6 of the Delhi Police (Punishment and Appeal) Rules, 1980, and check the current text of Rule 6 [(DP (P&A) Rules 5-6, PDF p. 17)](https://indiacode.gov.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/2188ca35-06ec-46d7-84ef-210bfa017c71/content#page=17).

faqs.q: Is censure a minor or a major penalty?
faqs.a: Censure is a minor penalty, listed first in Rule 11 [(Rule 11(i), PDF p. 10)](https://dopt.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCS-CCA-Rules-FINAL.pdf#page=10).

faqs.q: Is compulsory retirement always a penalty?
faqs.a: No. Compulsory retirement imposed as a penalty is a major penalty [(Rule 11(vii), PDF p. 11)](https://dopt.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCS-CCA-Rules-FINAL.pdf#page=11), but compulsory retirement under the superannuation or retirement provisions is not a penalty [(Rule 11, Explanation (vii), PDF p. 12)](https://dopt.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCS-CCA-Rules-FINAL.pdf#page=12).

faqs.q: What is the difference between removal and dismissal?
faqs.a: Removal is not a disqualification for future Government employment, while dismissal ordinarily is [(Rule 11(viii)-(ix), PDF p. 11)](https://dopt.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCS-CCA-Rules-FINAL.pdf#page=11).

faqs.q: Is stoppage at the efficiency bar a penalty?
faqs.a: No. Stopping you at the efficiency bar because you are unfit to cross it is not a penalty under Rule 11 [(Rule 11, Explanation (ii), PDF p. 11)](https://dopt.gov.in/sites/default/files/CCS-CCA-Rules-FINAL.pdf#page=11).
